title.zh: 卷15 列傳第7 寇洛 李弼 弟標 于謹 子寔
title.en: Volume 15 Biographies 7: Kou Luo; Li Bi; Di Biao; Yu Jin; Zi Shi
title.raw: 卷15 列傳第7 寇洛 李弼 弟標 于謹 子寔 Volume 15 Biographies 7: Kou Luo; Li Bi; Di Biao; Yu Jin; Zi Shi

sentences.zh: 寇洛 李弼 弟檦 于謹 子寔

translations.literal: Kou Luo; Li Bi; younger brother Biao; Yu Jin; Zi Shi
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo — Li Bi — younger brother Li Biao — Yu Jin — son Shi

sentences.zh: 寇洛，上谷昌平人，累世為將吏。

translations.literal: Kou Luo was a native of Changping in Shanggu; for generations his family had served as generals and officials.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo came from Changping in Shanggu; his forebears had been soldiers and officers for generations.

sentences.zh: 父延壽，和平中，以良家子鎮武川，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father Yanshou, in the Heping era, as a good-household youth garrisoned Wuchuan and settled his family there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanshou, posted to Wuchuan as a soldier of good family during the Heping era, made the town his home.

sentences.zh: 洛性明辨，不拘小節。

translations.literal: Luo by nature was bright and discerning and did not fuss over minor points.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo was clear-minded and quick to judge, and cared little for petty proprieties.

sentences.zh: 正光末，以北邊賊起，遂率鄉親避地於幷、肆，因從爾朱榮征討。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguang, because bandits rose on the northern frontier, he then led kinsmen and neighbors to seek refuge in Bing and Si, and followed Erzhu Rong on campaign and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenguang drew to a close and the northern border erupted in rebellion, he led his kin and neighbors into Bing and Si for safety, then entered Erzhu Rong's service on campaign.

sentences.zh: 及賀拔岳西征，洛與之鄉里，乃募從入關。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue marched west on campaign, Luo was a fellow townsman of his and therefore recruited followers to enter the Pass with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue marched west, Kou Luo—his townsman—raised men and followed him through the Pass into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 破赤水蜀，以功拜中堅將軍、屯騎校尉、別將，封臨邑縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Defeating the Chishui Shu, for merit he was appointed General of the Central Army, Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry, and separate commander; enfeoffed as Baron of Linyi county, fief two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After breaking the Chishui Shu he was made general of the central army, colonel of the garrison cavalry, and separate commander, and enfeoffed Baron of Linyi with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又從岳獲賊帥尉遲菩薩於渭水，破侯伏侯元進於百里細川，擒万俟醜奴於長坑。

translations.literal: Again following Yue, he captured the bandit chief Yuchi Pusa on the Wei River, broke Houfu Hou Yuanjin at Baili Xichuan, and took Wanqi Chounu at Changkeng.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Yue, taking the rebel chief Yuchi Pusa on the Wei, routing Houfu Hou Yuanjin at Baili Xichuan, and capturing Wanqi Chounu at Changkeng.

sentences.zh: 洛每力戰，並有功。

translations.literal: Each time Luo fought with all his strength, and in every case there was merit.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo fought at the front every time and earned credit in every action.

sentences.zh: 加龍驤將軍、都督，進爵安鄉縣子，累遷征北將軍、衛將軍。

translations.literal: Advanced to Dragon-Courser General and area commander; promoted in rank to Viscount of Anxiang county; successively promoted to General Who Campaigns North and General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to dragon-courser general and area commander, raised to Viscount of Anxiang, and then to general who campaigns north and general of the guard.

sentences.zh: 於平涼，以洛為右都督。

translations.literal: At Pingliang, Luo was made right area commander.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingliang, Kou Luo was appointed right area commander.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅旣害岳，欲幷其衆。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue having already killed Yue, wished to absorb his host.
translations.idiomatic: Once Houmochen Yue had murdered Heba Yue, he tried to swallow his army whole.

sentences.zh: 時初喪元帥，軍中惶擾，洛于諸將之中，最為舊齒，素為衆所信，乃收集將士，志在復讐，共相糾合，遂全衆而反。

translations.literal: At the time they had just lost the commander-in-chief; within the army there was fear and turmoil. Among the generals Luo was the most senior in standing and had long been trusted by the host; he therefore gathered officers and soldiers, set his heart on vengeance, joined together with the others, and so preserved the whole force and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: The army had just lost its commander and was in panic. Kou Luo was the senior among the generals and the men trusted him; he rallied the troops, bent on revenge, welded them together, and brought the whole command safely back.

sentences.zh: 旣至原州，衆咸推洛為盟主，統岳之衆。

translations.literal: Having reached Yuanzhou, the host all pushed Luo as covenant leader to command Yue's host.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanzhou the soldiers unanimously chose Kou Luo as covenant leader to take command of Heba Yue's forces.

sentences.zh: 洛復自以非才，乃固辭，與趙貴等議迎太祖。

translations.literal: Luo again considered himself without the talent for it and therefore firmly declined; with Zhao Gui and the others he deliberated on welcoming the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo judged himself unfit for the role and refused firmly; with Zhao Gui and others he planned to welcome Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 魏帝以洛有全師之功，除武衛將軍。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor, because Luo had the merit of preserving the army intact, appointed him General of Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor made him general of martial guard for saving the army intact.

sentences.zh: 太祖至平涼，以洛為右大都督。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor reached Pingliang, he made Luo right grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai reached Pingliang, he appointed Kou Luo right grand commander.

sentences.zh: 從討侯莫陳悅，平之，拜涇州刺史。

translations.literal: Following in the suppression of Houmochen Yue, he pacified him and was appointed Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the campaign against Houmochen Yue, crushed him, and was made governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，進爵臨邑縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Luo was advanced in rank to Earl of Linyi county, fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew westward, Kou Luo was raised to Earl of Linyi with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋進位驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，進爵為公，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honorary Three Preceptorships; advanced in rank to Duke, fief increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand general of chariots and cavalry with honorary three preceptorships, advanced to duke, and given five hundred more households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 大統初，魏文帝詔曰：「往者侯莫陳悅遠同逆賊，潛害故清水公岳，志在兼幷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, Emperor Wen of Wei issued an edict saying: "Formerly Houmochen Yue from afar joined with rebel bandits and secretly harmed the late Duke of Qingshui, Yue, his intent being to absorb and merge.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Datong, Emperor Wen of Wei decreed: "Houmochen Yue once conspired with rebels and secretly killed the late Duke of Qingshui, Heba Yue, aiming to seize his command.

sentences.zh: 當時造次，物情驚駭。

translations.literal: At the time, in haste, popular feeling was shocked and terrified.
translations.idiomatic: In the sudden crisis the army and people were thrown into terror.

sentences.zh: 使持節、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、前涇州刺史、大都督、臨邑縣開國公寇洛，忠款自心，勳誠早立，遂能糾合義軍，以待大丞相。

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honorary Three Preceptorships, former Governor of Jing Province, Grand Commander, and Duke of Linyi county, Kou Luo, loyalty sincere from the heart, merit and fidelity established early, was able to gather righteous troops and await the Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo—bearer of the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry with honorary three preceptorships, former governor of Jing, grand commander, and Duke of Linyi—had shown loyal devotion from the first and rallied the loyal army to await the grand chancellor.

sentences.zh: 見危授命，推賢而奉，此而不賞，何以勸勵將來。

translations.literal: Facing peril he accepted the charge; he pushed forward the worthy and served them—if this is not rewarded, how can the future be encouraged and exhorted?
translations.idiomatic: He took command in danger and yielded to the better man—if such service goes unrewarded, what will move those who come after?

sentences.zh: 可加開府，進爵京兆郡公。

translations.literal: He may be granted the office of opening a government, and advanced in rank to Duke of Jingzhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be granted an opened government and raised to Duke of Jingzhao commandery."

sentences.zh: 」封洛母宋氏為襄城郡君。

translations.literal: " Luo's mother, the Lady Song, was enfeoffed as Lady of Xiangcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo's mother, Lady Song, was enfeoffed Lady of Xiangcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 又轉領軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made general of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 三年，出為華州刺史，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the third year, he went out as Governor of Hua Province and was additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was posted governor of Hua Province and given palace attendant as well.

sentences.zh: 與獨孤信復洛陽，移鎮弘農。

translations.literal: Together with Dugu Xin he recovered Luoyang and moved the garrison to Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: With Dugu Xin he retook Luoyang and shifted the garrison to Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 四年，從太祖與東魏戰於河橋。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he followed the Grand Progenitor in battle with Eastern Wei at Heqiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai against Eastern Wei at Heqiao.

sentences.zh: 軍還，洛率所部鎮東雍。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Luo led his command to garrison Eastern Yong.
translations.idiomatic: On the march back Kou Luo led his troops to garrison Eastern Yong.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒于鎮，時年五十三。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he died at his post, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died in command, at fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、侍中、都督雍華豳涇原三秦二岐十州諸軍事、太尉、尚書令、驃騎大將軍、雍州刺史，諡曰武。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the Three Qin and Two Qi of Yong, Hua, Bin, Jing, and Yuan—ten provinces in all—Grand Commandant, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Governor of Yong Province; posthumous title Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander-in-chief over ten provinces—Yong, Hua, Bin, Jing, Yuan, the Three Qin, and the Two Qi—grand commandant, director of the Masters of Writing, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and governor of Yong; his posthumous name was Wu (" Martial ").

sentences.zh: 子和嗣。

translations.literal: His son He succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son He succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 世宗二年，錄勳舊，以洛配享太祖廟庭，賜和姓若口引氏，改封松陽郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Shizong, when old merits were recorded, Luo was paired to share offerings in the Grand Progenitor's temple court; he was granted the He surname and the Ruokouyin clan, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Songyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Shizong's second year, when old services were honored, Kou Luo was paired to share offerings in Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's temple; he received the sinicized surname He and the clan name Ruokouyin, and his title was changed to Duke of Songyang.

sentences.zh: 後至開府儀同三司、賓部中大夫。

translations.literal: Later he reached Honorary Three Preceptorships with an office and Grand Master of the Guest Section.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to honorary three preceptorships with an office and grand master of the guest section.

sentences.zh: 洛弟紹，位至上柱國、北平郡公。

translations.literal: Luo's younger brother Shao rose to Senior Pillar of State and Duke of Beiping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo's younger brother Shao rose to senior pillar of state and Duke of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 李弼字景和，遼東襄平人也。

translations.literal: Li Bi, styled Jinghe, was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi, styled Jinghe, came from Xiangping in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 六世祖根，慕容垂黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Gen served Murong Chui as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations back his forebear Gen had been attendant gentleman at the yellow gate under Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 祖貴醜，平州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guichou was Governor of Ping Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guichou was governor of Ping Province.

sentences.zh: 父永，太中大夫，贈涼州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yong was Grand Master of Palace Counsel and was posthumously awarded Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong was grand master of palace counsel and was posthumously made governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 弼少有大志，膂力過人。

translations.literal: Bi from youth had great ambition; his physical strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi had been ambitious from boyhood, and his strength outmatched ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 屬魏室喪亂，語所親曰：「丈夫生世，會須履鋒刃，平寇難，安社稷以取功名；

translations.literal: At a time when the Wei house was in disorder and ruin, he said to those close to him: "When a man is born into the world, he ought to tread the sharp edge, pacify bandits and calamity, settle the altars of soil and grain, and thereby win merit and fame;
translations.idiomatic: While the Wei court collapsed in chaos he told his intimates: "A man born into this age should walk the blade's edge—crush rebels, save the realm, and win a name worth keeping;

sentences.zh: 安能碌碌依階資以求榮位乎。

translations.literal: How can one drudge along, relying on step-by-step seniority to seek rank and glory?
translations.idiomatic: not creep up the ladder of seniority begging for office."

sentences.zh: 」魏永安元年，爾朱天光辟為別將，從天光西討，破赤水蜀。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Yongan of Wei, Erzhu Tianguang recruited him as separate commander; following Tianguang on the western campaign, he broke the Chishui Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Yongan 1 (528) Erzhu Tianguang took him on as separate commander; on the western campaign he broke the Chishui Shu.

sentences.zh: 以功拜征虜將軍，封石門縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed General Who Captures the Barbarians and enfeoffed Earl of Shimen county, fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made general who captures the barbarians and enfeoffed Earl of Shimen with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又與賀拔岳討万俟醜奴、万俟道洛、王慶雲，皆破之。

translations.literal: Again with Heba Yue he suppressed Wanqi Chounu, Wanqi Daoluo, and Wang Qingyun—all were broken.
translations.idiomatic: He again campaigned with Heba Yue against Wanqi Chounu, Wanqi Daoluo, and Wang Qingyun, and routed them all.

sentences.zh: 弼恆先鋒陷陣，所向披靡，賊咸畏之，曰「莫當李將軍前也」。

translations.literal: Bi always as vanguard broke the formations; wherever he turned the enemy were scattered; the bandits all feared him and said, "Do not stand before General Li."
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi always led the van and smashed the enemy line; nothing stood before him. The rebels feared him and said, "No one blocks General Li."

sentences.zh: 天光赴洛，弼因隸侯莫陳悅，為大都督，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Tianguang went to Luoyang; Bi thereupon came under Houmochen Yue as grand commander and was additionally made Regular Attendant through Direct Connection.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang marched to Luoyang, Li Bi entered Houmochen Yue's service as grand commander and was given regular attendant through direct connection as well.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang,
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang,

translations.literal: (Shou) [emended: appointed]
translations.idiomatic: he was appointed

sentences.zh: 〔授〕清水郡守，恆州大中正。

translations.literal: Governor of Qingshui commandery, Heng Province senior arbitrator.
translations.idiomatic: governor of Qingshui commandery and senior arbitrator of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 尋除南秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon removed as Governor of Southern Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Southern Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 隨悅征討，屢有剋捷。

translations.literal: Following Yue on campaign and suppression, repeatedly there were captures and victories.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign under Houmochen Yue he won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 及悅害賀拔岳，軍停隴上。

translations.literal: When Yue killed Heba Yue, the army halted on Long.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue murdered Heba Yue, the army stopped on the Long plateau.

sentences.zh: 太祖自平涼進軍討悅。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor advanced his army from Pingliang to suppress Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched from Pingliang to punish Houmochen Yue.

sentences.zh: 弼諫悅曰：「嶽旣無罪而公害之，又不能撫納其衆，使無所歸。

translations.literal: Bi remonstrated with Yue, saying: "Yue was without guilt yet the Duke harmed him, and moreover could not soothe and accept his host, leaving them with nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi warned Houmochen Yue: "Heba Yue was innocent, yet you killed him and failed to hold his men—they have nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 宇文夏州收而用之，得其死力，咸雲為主將報讐，其意固不小也。

translations.literal: Yuwen, Commander of Xia Province, has gathered and employed them and gained their strength unto death; all say they fight to avenge their commander—their intent is certainly no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai of Xia Province has taken them in and won their absolute loyalty; they mean to avenge their general—that purpose is no small thing.

sentences.zh: 今宜解兵謝之，不然，恐必受禍。

translations.literal: Now you ought to disband your troops and apologize to him; otherwise, I fear you will surely meet disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Disband your army and make amends, or you will surely come to ruin."

sentences.zh: 」悅惶惑，計無所出。

translations.literal: " Yue was alarmed and confused, with no plan to get out.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue panicked and could find no way out.

sentences.zh: 弼知悅必敗，乃謂所親曰：「宇文夏州才略冠世，德義可宗。

translations.literal: Bi knew Yue would surely be defeated and therefore said to those close to him: "Yuwen, Commander of Xia Province, in talent and strategy crowns the age; in virtue and righteousness he may be taken as model.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi saw that Houmochen Yue was doomed and told his intimates: "Yuwen Tai of Xia Province is the foremost man of the age in talent and the standard of honor.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳公智小謀大，豈能自保。

translations.literal: The Duke of Houmochen is small in wisdom yet large in plotting—how can he preserve himself?
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue is clever in small things and reckless in large ones—how can he save himself?

sentences.zh: 吾等若不為計，恐與之同至族滅。

translations.literal: If we do not make plans for ourselves, I fear we shall together reach clan extermination.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not act for ourselves, we will be wiped out with him."

sentences.zh: 」會太祖軍至，悅乃棄秦州南出，據險以自固。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor's army arrived, Yue then abandoned Qin Province and marched south, holding perilous ground to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's army arrived, Houmochen Yue abandoned Qin Province, fled south, and dug in on difficult ground.

sentences.zh: 翌日，弼密通使太祖，許背悅來降。

translations.literal: The next day, Bi secretly sent envoys to the Grand Progenitor, promising to turn against Yue and come over.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Li Bi secretly sent word to Yuwen Tai, offering to betray Houmochen Yue and defect.

sentences.zh: 夜，弼乃勒所部云：「侯莫陳公欲還秦州，汝等何不束裝？

translations.literal: At night, Bi then ordered his command, saying: "The Duke of Houmochen wishes to return to Qin Province—why do you not pack your gear?
translations.idiomatic: That night he told his troops: "Houmochen Yue means to march back to Qin Province—pack your kit at once!

sentences.zh: 」弼妻，悅之姨也，特為悅所親委，衆咸信之。

translations.literal: " Bi's wife was Yue's maternal cousin and was especially trusted and entrusted by Yue; the host all believed her.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Bi's wife was Houmochen Yue's cousin by marriage and one he trusted completely; the men believed her.

sentences.zh: 人情驚擾，不可復定，皆散走，爭趣秦州。

translations.literal: Popular feeling was alarmed and unsettled and could not again be stabilized; all scattered and fled, competing to rush toward Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread; order broke; the soldiers bolted, all racing for Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 弼乃先馳據城門以慰輯之，遂擁衆以歸太祖。

translations.literal: Bi then first galloped ahead to seize the city gate and soothe and gather them; he thereupon led the host to return to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi rode ahead, seized the gate, calmed the fugitives, and led the whole command over to Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 悅由此遂敗。

translations.literal: Yue for this reason was then defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue was ruined by it.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂弼曰：「公與吾同心，天下不足平也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said to Bi: "If you and I are of one mind, the realm under Heaven is not hard to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai told Li Bi: "With you and me of one mind, the realm is not hard to conquer."

sentences.zh: 」破悅，得金寶奴婢，悉以好者賜之。

translations.literal: " Having broken Yue, he obtained gold, jewels, slaves, and maidservants and entirely gave the fine ones to him as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: After crushing Houmochen Yue he took gold, jewels, slaves, and maidservants and gave Li Bi the best of them.

sentences.zh: 仍令弼以本官鎮原州。

translations.literal: He still ordered Bi, with his existing office, to garrison Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left Li Bi at Yuanzhou in his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 尋拜秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 太祖率兵東下，徵弼為大都督，領右軍，攻潼關及迴洛城，剋之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor led troops east; Bi was summoned as grand commander, commanding the right army, attacking Tong Pass and Huiluo city—both were taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai marched east he called Li Bi as grand commander of the right wing; they took Tong Pass and Huiluo.

sentences.zh: 大統初，進位儀同三司、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, promoted to Honorary Three Preceptorships and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Datong he was made honorary three preceptorships and governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 尋又進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon again promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Honorary Three Preceptorships with an opened government.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to grand general of chariots and cavalry with an opened government of honorary three preceptorships.

sentences.zh: 從平竇泰，先鋒陷敵，斬獲居多。

translations.literal: Following in the pacification of Dou Tai, as vanguard he broke the enemy; beheadings and captures were the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign that brought down Dou Tai he led the van, shattered the foe, and took the lion's share of heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 太祖以所乘騅馬及竇泰所著牟甲賜弼。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor gave Bi the piebald horse he himself rode and the mail armor Dou Tai had worn as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai gave him his own piebald mount and the mail Dou Tai had worn.

sentences.zh: 又從平弘農。

translations.literal: Again following in the pacification of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the pacification of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 與齊神武戰於沙苑，弼率軍居右，而左軍為敵所乘。

translations.literal: Battling Gao Huan at Shayuan, Bi led the army on the right, while the left army was struck by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At Shayuan against Gao Huan, Li Bi held the right while the left wing was overrun.

sentences.zh: 弼呼其麾下六十騎，身先士卒，橫截之，賊遂為

translations.literal: Bi called his sixty riders under him, took the lead before the soldiers, and cut across them; the bandits then were
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi rallied his sixty horsemen, led from the front, and charged across the enemy flank; the foe was

translations.literal: (San) [emended: scattered]
translations.idiomatic: scattered;

sentences.zh: ，因大破。

translations.literal: , and so were routed in a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: split apart, and he broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 以功拜特進，爵趙郡公，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: For merit appointed Special Grand Master; enfeoffed Duke of Zhao commandery; fief increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made special grand master, enfeoffed Duke of Zhao commandery, and given one thousand more households.

sentences.zh: 又與賀拔勝攻克河東，略定汾、絳。

translations.literal: Again with Heba Sheng he captured Hedong and broadly settled Fen and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: With Heba Sheng he took Hedong and broadly pacified Fen and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 四年，從太祖東討洛陽，弼為前驅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, following the Grand Progenitor on the eastern campaign against Luoyang, Bi served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai east against Luoyang as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 東魏將莫多婁貸文率衆數千，奄至穀城。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei general Modu Lou Daiwen led a host of several thousand and suddenly arrived at Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei general Modu Lou Daiwen came suddenly on Gucheng with several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 弼倍道而前，遣軍士鼓噪，曳柴揚塵。

translations.literal: Bi, marching at double pace, sent soldiers to beat drums and shout, dragging brushwood to raise dust.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi forced the march, had his men drum and shout, and dragged brushwood to raise a dust cloud.

sentences.zh: 貸文以為大軍至，遂遁走。

translations.literal: Daiwen thought the main army had arrived and therefore fled and went away.
translations.idiomatic: Daiwen took it for the main army and fled.

sentences.zh: 弼追躡之，虜其衆，斬貸文，傳首大軍所。

translations.literal: Bi pursued and followed on his heels, captured his host, beheaded Daiwen, and sent the head to the main army's position.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi chased him down, took his force, beheaded Daiwen, and sent the head to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 翌日，又從太祖與齊神武戰於河橋，每入深陷陣，身被七創，遂為所獲，圍守數重。

translations.literal: The next day, again following the Grand Progenitor in battle with Gao Huan at Heqiao, each time he entered deep and broke the formations; his body received seven wounds; he was then captured by them and besieged within many rings.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he again followed Yuwen Tai against Gao Huan at Heqiao, plunging deep into the enemy line again and again until he took seven wounds, was taken, and lay trapped under ring after ring of guards.

sentences.zh: 弼佯若創重，殞絕於地。

translations.literal: Bi pretended that his wounds were grave and collapsed dead to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi feigned mortal wounds and dropped as if dead.

sentences.zh: 守者稍懈，弼睨其旁有馬，因躍上西馳，得免。

translations.literal: The guards gradually slackened; Bi glanced and saw a horse beside him, leaped onto it, and galloped west—he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When the guards relaxed he spotted a horse nearby, vaulted onto it, and galloped west to freedom.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷司空。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 六年，侯景據荊州，弼與獨孤信禦之，景乃退走。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Hou Jing held Jing Province; Bi together with Dugu Xin defended against him, and Jing then withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Hou Jing seized Jing Province; Li Bi and Dugu Xin held him off until Hou Jing broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 九年，從戰邙山，轉太尉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, following in battle at Mount Mang, transferred to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, at the battle of Mount Mang, he was transferred to grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 十三年，侯景率河南六州來附，東魏遣其將韓軌圍景於潁川。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Hou Jing led the six provinces of Henan to come and submit; Eastern Wei sent its general Han Gui to besiege Jing at Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Hou Jing brought the six Henan provinces over to the Zhou side; Eastern Wei sent Han Gui to besiege him at Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣弼率軍援景，諸將咸受弼節度。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor dispatched Bi to lead an army to relieve Jing; the generals all received Bi's command and control.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent Li Bi to relieve Hou Jing; every general on the field came under his orders.

sentences.zh: 弼至，軌退。

translations.literal: When Bi arrived, Gui withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bi arrived, Han Gui pulled back.

sentences.zh: 王思政又進據潁川，弼乃引還。

translations.literal: Wang Sizheng again advanced and held Yingchuan; Bi then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng again advanced and occupied Yingchuan; Li Bi then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十四年，北稽胡反，弼討平之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the northern Ji Hu rebelled; Bi suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the northern Ji Hu rose in revolt; Li Bi suppressed and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 遷太保，加柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Preceptor and additionally made Pillar-of-State Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Preceptor and additionally Pillar-of-State Grand General.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，賜姓徒河氏。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Deposed Emperor of Wei, he was granted the surname Tuhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Deposed Emperor of Wei (551), he was granted the surname Tuhe.

sentences.zh: 太祖西巡，令弼居守，後事皆諮稟焉。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke toured the west and had Bi remain on guard; all subsequent affairs were referred to him for consultation and report.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai toured the west, he had Li Bi remain on guard; all later business was referred to him for counsel.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜太傅、大司徒。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Grand Tutor and Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Grand Tutor and Grand Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 屬茹茹為突厥所逼，舉國請降，弼率前軍迎之。

translations.literal: At the time the Rouran, pressed by the Turks, submitted the whole state in surrender; Bi led the vanguard to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran, hard pressed by the Turks, surrendered the whole state, Li Bi led the vanguard to receive them.

sentences.zh: 給前後部羽葆鼓吹，賜雜彩六千段。

translations.literal: He was granted front and rear guard of feathered canopy and drums and bugles, and given six thousand bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted front and rear guard of feathered canopy with drums and bugles, and given six thousand bolts of mixed silks.

sentences.zh: 及晉公護執政，朝之大事，皆與于謹及弼等參議。

translations.literal: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held the government, all major state affairs were deliberated with Yu Jin and Bi and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held power, all major affairs of state were deliberated with Yu Jin, Li Bi, and others.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，除太師，進封趙國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Bi was made Grand Preceptor and advanced to Duke of Zhao state, fief ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Li Bi was made Grand Preceptor and advanced to Duke of Zhao with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 前後賞賜累巨萬。

translations.literal: Rewards and grants before and after accumulated to vast sums.
translations.idiomatic: Grants and rewards over the years amounted to enormous sums.

sentences.zh: 子

translations.literal: Son
translations.idiomatic: His sons:

translations.literal: (Hui)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Hui]

translations.literal: [Yao].
translations.idiomatic: Yao.

sentences.zh: 次子

translations.literal: Second son
translations.idiomatic: The second son

translations.literal: (Yao)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Yao]

sentences.zh: 〔輝〕，尚太祖女義安長公主，遂以為嗣。

translations.literal: [Hui], married the Grand Duke's daughter the Princess Chang of Yi'an, and was thus made heir.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, who married Yuwen Tai's daughter the Princess Chang of Yi'an, was made heir.

translations.literal: (Hui)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Hui]

sentences.zh: 〔耀〕旣不得為嗣，朝廷以弼功重，乃封

translations.literal: [Yao], since he could not be made heir, the court on account of Bi's great merits then enfeoffed
translations.idiomatic: Yao, since he could not be made heir, the court—on account of Li Bi's great service—then enfeoffed

translations.literal: (Hui)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Hui]

sentences.zh: 〔耀〕邢國公，位至開府。

translations.literal: [Yao] as Duke of Xing state, reaching the rank of opening-the-feudatory.
translations.idiomatic: Yao as Duke of Xing with the rank of opening-the-feudatory.

sentences.zh: 子寬，大象末，上大將軍蒲山郡公。

translations.literal: His son Kuan, at the end of Daxiang, was made Grand General and Duke of Puzhan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuan, at the end of Daxiang (581), was made grand general and Duke of Puzhan commandery.

sentences.zh: 輝弟衍，大象末，大將軍、真鄉郡公。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Yan, at the end of Daxiang, was Grand General and Duke of Zhenxiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Yan, at the end of Daxiang, was grand general and Duke of Zhenxiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 衍弟綸，最知名，有文武才用。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Lun was the most renowned, with civil and military talent and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Lun was the best known, talented in both civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 以功臣子，少居顯職，歷吏部、內史下大夫，竝獲當官之譽。

translations.literal: As the son of a meritorious minister, from youth he held prominent posts, serving as lower grand master in the Ministry of Personnel and in the Secretariat, and in both gained the reputation of a capable official.
translations.idiomatic: As a meritorious minister's son he held high office from youth, serving as lower grand master in the Ministry of Personnel and in the Secretariat, and in both won praise as a capable official.

sentences.zh: 位至司會中大夫、開府儀同三司，封河陽郡公。

translations.literal: He reached the posts of Middle Grand Master of the Bureau of Accounts and Opening-the-Feudatory Three Preceptorships, and was enfeoffed Duke of Heyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to middle grand master of the Bureau of Accounts and opening-the-feudatory with Three Preceptorships, and was enfeoffed Duke of Heyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 為聘齊使主。

translations.literal: He served as chief envoy on a mission to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He headed the embassy to Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 子長雅嗣。

translations.literal: His son Changya succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changya succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 綸弟晏，建德中，開府儀同三司、大將軍、趙郡公。

translations.literal: Lun's younger brother Yan, during Jiande, was Opening-the-Feudatory Three Preceptorships, Grand General, and Duke of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's younger brother Yan, during Jiande (572–578), was opening-the-feudatory with Three Preceptorships, grand general, and Duke of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 從高祖平齊，歿於幷州。

translations.literal: He followed the High Ancestor in pacifying Qi and died at Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu (Yuwen Yong) in the conquest of Qi and died at Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 子璟以晏死王事，卽襲其爵。

translations.literal: His son Jing, because Yan died in the king's service, immediately inherited his title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing, because Yan died in imperial service, at once inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 弼弟檦。

translations.literal: Bi's younger brother Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi's younger brother Di Biao.

sentences.zh: 檦字靈傑。

translations.literal: Biao, styled Lingjie.
translations.idiomatic: Di Biao, styled Lingjie.

sentences.zh: 長不盈五尺，性果決，有膽氣。

translations.literal: In height he did not reach five chi; by nature he was resolute and had daring spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He stood less than five chi tall, but was resolute by nature and full of daring.

sentences.zh: 少事爾朱榮。

translations.literal: From youth he served Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he served Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 魏永安元年，以兼別將從榮破元顥，拜討逆將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongan of Wei, as acting separate commander he followed Rong in defeating Yuan Hao and was appointed General Who Punishes Rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongan of Wei (528), as acting separate commander he followed Erzhu Rong in defeating Yuan Hao and was appointed General Who Punishes Rebellion.

sentences.zh: 及榮被害，檦從爾朱世隆奉榮妻奔河北。

translations.literal: When Rong was killed, Biao followed Erzhu Shilong in escorting Rong's wife in flight to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong was killed, Di Biao followed Erzhu Shilong in escorting Rong's wife to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 又隨爾朱兆入洛。

translations.literal: He again followed Erzhu Zhao into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Erzhu Zhao into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 賜爵淝城郡男，遷都督。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Baron of Feicheng commandery and transferred to commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Baron of Feicheng commandery and made a commander.

sentences.zh: 普泰元年，元樹自梁入據譙城，檦從行臺樊子鵠擊破之，遷右將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putai, Yuan Shu came from Liang and held Qiao city; Biao followed Mobile Corps Commander Fan Zihu in defeating him and was transferred to General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putai (531), Yuan Shu came from Liang and seized Qiao; Di Biao followed Mobile Corps Commander Fan Zihu in defeating him and was transferred to General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，檦從大都督元斌之與齊神武戰於成皋。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Biao followed Grand Commander Yuan Binzhi in fighting Qi Shenwu at Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Di Biao followed Grand Commander Yuan Binzhi in fighting Gao Huan at Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 兵敗，遂與斌之奔梁。

translations.literal: The army was defeated; he then fled to Liang with Binzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The army was beaten; he fled to Liang with Yuan Binzhi.

sentences.zh: 梁主待以賓禮，後得逃歸。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler treated him with guest rites; later he was able to escape and return.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor received him as an honored guest; later he escaped and returned.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，授撫軍將軍，進封晉陽縣子，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and advanced to Viscount of Jinyang county, fief four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong (535), he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and advanced to Viscount of Jinyang with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋為太祖帳內都督。

translations.literal: Soon he became commander within the Grand Duke's tent guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became a commander in Yuwen Tai's personal guard.

sentences.zh: 從復弘農，破沙苑。

translations.literal: He followed in recovering Hongnong and defeating [the enemy] at Shaya.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in recovering Hongnong and in the victory at Shaya.

sentences.zh: 檦跨馬運矛，衝鋒陷陣，隱身鞍甲之中。

translations.literal: Biao, astride his horse wielding his spear, charged the van and broke formations, his body hidden among saddle and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Di Biao rode with spear in hand, charging the van and breaking ranks, his small frame hidden among saddle and armor.

sentences.zh: 敵人見之，皆曰「避此小兒」。

translations.literal: Enemies who saw him all said, "Avoid this little boy."
translations.idiomatic: Enemies who saw him all cried, "Keep clear of that boy!"

sentences.zh: 不知檦之形貌，正自如是。

translations.literal: They did not know that Biao's appearance was exactly like this.
translations.idiomatic: They did not know that Di Biao's appearance was exactly like this.

sentences.zh: 太祖初亦聞檦驍悍，未見其能，至是方嗟歎之。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke at first had also heard of Biao's fierce valor but had not seen his ability; only now did he sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai had long heard of Di Biao's fierce reputation but had not seen him fight; only now did he sigh in admiration.

sentences.zh: 謂檦曰：「但使膽決如此，何必須要八尺之軀也。

translations.literal: He said to Biao: "If one has daring and resolve like this, why must one need an eight-chi frame?
translations.idiomatic: He told Di Biao: "With courage and resolve like this, who needs an eight-chi frame?

sentences.zh: 」以功進爵為公，增邑四百戶。

translations.literal: " For merit he was advanced in rank to duke and his fief increased by four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: " For his service he was advanced to duke and his fief increased by four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋從宇文貴與東魏將任祥、堯雄等戰於潁川，皆破之。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Yuwen Gui in fighting Eastern Wei generals Ren Xiang, Yao Xiong, and others at Yingchuan, and all were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he followed Yuwen Gui in fighting Eastern Wei generals Ren Xiang, Yao Xiong, and others at Yingchuan and defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 徵為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as junior mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as junior mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 九年，從戰邙山，遷持節、大都督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he followed the campaign at Mount Mang and was transferred to Bearer of the Staff and Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he fought at Mount Mang and was transferred to bearer of the staff and grand commander.

sentences.zh: 十三年，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Opening-the-Feudatory Three Preceptorships.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and opening-the-feudatory with Three Preceptorships.

sentences.zh: 又從弼討稽胡，檦功居多，除幽州刺史，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: He again followed Bi in suppressing the Ji Hu; Biao's merit was the greatest, and he was made governor of You Province with fief increased by three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Li Bi against the Ji Hu; Di Biao's merit was greatest, and he was made governor of You Province with a fief increase of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十五年，拜驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was appointed Grand General of Cavalry and Opening-the-Feudatory Three Preceptorships.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Grand General of Cavalry and opening-the-feudatory with Three Preceptorships.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝初，從趙貴征茹茹，論功為最，改封封山縣公，增邑幷前二千一百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor of Wei, he followed Zhao Gui in campaigning against the Rouran; in reckoning merit he ranked first, was transferred to Duke of Fengshan county, and his fief together with the previous total reached two thousand one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he followed Zhao Gui against the Rouran; judged foremost in merit, he was transferred to Duke of Fengshan with a combined fief of two thousand one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was advanced to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was advanced to grand general.

sentences.zh: 武成初，又從豆盧寧征稽胡，大獲而還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, he again followed Dou Lu Ning in campaigning against the Ji Hu and returned with great gains.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng (559) he again followed Dou Lu Ning against the Ji Hu and returned with rich spoils.

sentences.zh: 進爵汝南郡公。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to Duke of Runan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Duke of Runan commandery.

sentences.zh: 出為總管延綏丹三州諸軍事、延州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as grand commander of Yan, Sui, and Dan provinces military affairs and governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as grand commander over military affairs of Yan, Sui, and Dan provinces and governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he died at his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈恆朔等五州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded the governorships of Heng, Shuo, and four other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was awarded the governorships of Heng, Shuo, and four other provinces.

sentences.zh: 檦無子，以弼子椿嗣。

translations.literal: Biao had no sons; Bi's son Chun succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Di Biao had no sons; Li Bi's son Chun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 先以檦勳功，封魏平縣子。

translations.literal: Earlier, on account of Biao's merit, [Chun] was enfeoffed Viscount of Weiping county.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, for Di Biao's service, Chun had been enfeoffed Viscount of Weiping county.

sentences.zh: 大象末，開府儀同三司、大將軍、右宮伯，改封河東郡公。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, [he was] Opening-the-Feudatory Three Preceptorships, Grand General, and Right Palace Steward, transferred to Duke of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daxiang he was opening-the-feudatory with Three Preceptorships, grand general, and right palace steward, and was transferred to Duke of Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 于謹字思敬，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yu Jin, styled Sijing, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin, styled Sijing, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 小名巨彌。

translations.literal: His childhood name was Jumi.
translations.idiomatic: His childhood name was Jumi.

sentences.zh: 曾祖婆，魏懷荒鎮將。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Po was garrison commander of Huaihuang in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Po was garrison commander of Huaihuang under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖安定，平涼郡守、高平郡將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Anding was governor of Pingliang commandery and commandant of Gaoping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Anding was governor of Pingliang commandery and commandant of Gaoping commandery.

sentences.zh: 父提，隴西郡守，荏平縣伯。

translations.literal: His father Ti was governor of Longxi commandery and Baron of Renping county.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ti was governor of Longxi commandery and Baron of Renping county.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，以謹著勳，追贈使持節、柱國大將軍、太保、建平郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, on account of Jin's outstanding merit, [Ti was] posthumously awarded Bearer of the Staff, Pillar-of-State Grand General, Grand Preceptor, and Duke of Jianping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding (562), for Yu Jin's distinguished service, Ti was posthumously made bearer of the staff, pillar-of-state grand general, grand preceptor, and Duke of Jianping commandery.

sentences.zh: 謹性沉深，有識量，略窺經史，尤好《孫子兵書》。

translations.literal: Jin's nature was deep and reserved, with discernment and capacity; he had glanced at the classics and histories and especially loved Sunzi's Art of War.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin was deep and reserved, with judgment and breadth of mind; he had read the classics and histories and especially loved Sunzi's Art of War.

sentences.zh: 屏居閭里，未有仕進之志。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion in his village and had no ambition for office and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He lived quietly in his home village and had no wish to enter official life.

sentences.zh: 或有勸之者，謹曰：「州郡之職，昔人所鄙，台鼎之位，須待時來。

translations.literal: When some urged him, Jin said: "The posts of prefecture and commandery are what men of old despised; the seats at the imperial table must await the right time.
translations.idiomatic: When some urged him on, Yu Jin said: "Prefectural posts are what men of old looked down on; a place at the imperial table must wait its season.

sentences.zh: 吾所以優遊郡邑，聊以卒歲耳。

translations.literal: That is why I wander at ease in the district towns, simply to pass the year."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I take my ease in the county towns, simply to live out the year."

sentences.zh: 」太宰元穆見之，歎曰：「王佐材也。」

translations.literal: " Grand Preceptor Yuan Mu saw him and sighed: "Material for a king's assistant."
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Preceptor Yuan Mu met him and sighed: "Here is material for a king's right hand."

sentences.zh: 及破六汗拔陵首亂北境，引茹茹為援，大行臺僕射元纂率衆討之。

translations.literal: When Poliuhan Balang first raised disorder on the northern frontier and brought the Rouran as allies, Mobile Corps Vice Director Yuan Zuan led troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Poliuhan Balang first raised rebellion on the northern frontier and called in the Rouran as allies, Mobile Corps Vice Director Yuan Zuan led troops against him.

sentences.zh: 宿聞謹名，辟為鎧曹參軍事，從軍北伐。

translations.literal: Having long heard Jin's name, [Zuan] recruited him as aide in the Armor Bureau and followed the army on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Having long heard Yu Jin's name, Yuan Zuan recruited him as aide in the Armor Bureau and took him on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 茹茹聞大軍之逼，遂逃出塞。

translations.literal: The Rouran, hearing of the great army's approach, then fled out of the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran, hearing the main army approach, fled beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 纂令謹率二千騎追之，至郁對原，前後十七戰，盡降其衆。

translations.literal: Zuan ordered Jin to lead two thousand cavalry in pursuit; reaching Yudui Plain, in seventeen battles before and after, he fully subdued their host.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zuan ordered Yu Jin to pursue with two thousand cavalry; at Yudui Plain, in seventeen engagements, he brought the whole force to surrender.

sentences.zh: 後率輕騎出塞覘賊，屬鐵勒數千騎奄至，謹以衆寡不敵，退必不免，乃散其衆騎，使匿叢薄之間，又遣人升山指麾，若分部軍衆者。

translations.literal: Later he led light cavalry out of the passes to reconnoiter the enemy; when several thousand Tiele cavalry suddenly arrived, Jin, considering his force too few to match them and that retreat would surely not escape, then scattered his cavalry and had them hide among thickets, and also sent men up a hill to signal commands as if dividing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Later he led light cavalry beyond the passes to scout the enemy; when several thousand Tiele horsemen suddenly appeared, Yu Jin saw that he was too few to fight and could not escape by flight. He scattered his riders to hide in the brush and sent men up a hill to signal commands as if deploying troops in sections.

sentences.zh: 賊望見，雖疑有伏兵，旣恃其衆，不以為慮，乃進軍逼謹。

translations.literal: The enemy saw this; though they suspected an ambush, since they relied on their numbers they did not take it to heart and advanced to press Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy saw this; though they suspected an ambush, trusting in their numbers they paid it little heed and pressed on toward Yu Jin.

sentences.zh: 謹以常乘駿馬一紫一騧，賊先所識，乃使二人各乘一馬，突陣而出。

translations.literal: Jin, since he regularly rode fine horses, one purple and one piebald, which the enemy had previously recognized, then had two men each ride one horse and burst through the formation and out.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin usually rode a pair of fine horses, one purple and one piebald, which the enemy knew well; he had two men mount them and break through the line.

sentences.zh: 賊以為謹也，皆爭逐之。

translations.literal: The enemy thought it was Jin and all vied in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy thought it was Yu Jin and all gave chase.

sentences.zh: 謹乃率餘軍擊之，其追騎遂奔走，因得入塞。

translations.literal: Jin then led the remaining army to strike them; the pursuing cavalry thereupon fled, and he was thus able to enter the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin then led the rest of his force against them; the pursuers broke and fled, and he got back inside the frontier.

sentences.zh: 正光四年，行臺廣陽王元深治兵北伐，引謹為長流參軍，特相禮接。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguang, Mobile Corps Prince of Guangyang Yuan Shen drilled troops for the northern campaign and brought Jin in as senior flowing aide, treating him with special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguang (523), Mobile Corps Prince of Guangyang Yuan Shen mustered troops for a northern campaign and took Yu Jin as senior flowing aide, treating him with marked favor.

sentences.zh: 所有謀議，皆與謹參之。

translations.literal: All planning and deliberation were shared with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: All counsel and planning were shared with Yu Jin.

sentences.zh: 乃使其子佛陁拜焉，其見待如此。

translations.literal: He even had his son Fotuo pay respects to him; such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: He even had his son Fotuo pay him formal respects; such was the favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 遂與廣陽王破賊主斛律野穀祿等。

translations.literal: He then together with the Prince of Guangyang defeated the bandit chieftain Holü Yehulu and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the Prince of Guangyang in defeating the rebel chieftain Holü Yehulu and others.

sentences.zh: 時魏末亂，羣盜蜂起，謹乃從容謂廣陽王曰：「自正光以後，海內沸騰，郡國荒殘，農商廢業。

translations.literal: At the time, in the disorder at the end of Wei, bandits swarmed everywhere; Jin then said calmly to the Prince of Guangyang: "Since Zhenguang, within the seas turmoil has boiled; commanderies and states lie waste, and farming and trade have ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos at the end of Wei, bandits rose everywhere; Yu Jin then said calmly to the Prince of Guangyang: "Since Zhenguang the realm has seethed with disorder; commanderies and districts lie in ruins and farming and trade are dead.

sentences.zh: 今殿下奉義行誅，遠臨關塞，然丑類蟻聚，其徒實繁，若極武窮兵，恐非計之上者。

translations.literal: Now Your Highness, upholding righteousness in punitive campaign, comes from afar to the frontier passes; yet the wicked sort swarm like ants and their followers are truly numerous. If one exhausts force in extreme warfare, I fear that is not the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness now comes on a righteous punitive campaign to the frontier passes, but the wicked swarm like ants and their numbers are great. To use every last weapon may not be the wisest course.

sentences.zh: 謹願稟大王之威略，馳往喻之，必不勞兵甲，可致清蕩。

translations.literal: Jin wishes to rely on Your Highness's authority and strategy, ride swiftly to instruct them, and surely without troubling arms and armor can bring about complete pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Let me ride out under Your Highness's authority and persuade them; I am sure we can pacify them without drawing sword or spear.

sentences.zh: 」廣陽王然之。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Guangyang agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince of Guangyang agreed.

sentences.zh: 謹兼解諸國語，乃單騎入賊，示以恩信。

translations.literal: Jin also understood the languages of the various states; he then entered the bandits alone on horseback and showed them favor and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin also knew the languages of the frontier peoples; he rode alone into the rebel camp and offered them grace and good faith.

sentences.zh: 於是西部鐵勒酋長乜列河等，領三萬餘戶並款附，相率南遷。

translations.literal: Thereupon the western Tiele chieftain Mieliehe and others, leading more than thirty thousand households, all submitted in good faith and in succession moved south.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the western Tiele chieftain Mieliehe and others, leading more than thirty thousand households, all came over in submission and moved south in succession.

sentences.zh: 廣陽王欲與謹至折敷嶺迎接之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangyang wished to go with Jin to Zhefu Ridge to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangyang wished to go with Yu Jin to Zhefu Ridge to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 謹曰：「破六汗拔陵兵衆不少，聞乜列河等歸附，必來要擊。

translations.literal: Jin said: "Poliuhan Balang's troops are not few; hearing that Mieliehe and others have submitted, he will surely come to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin said: "Poliuhan Balang's force is large; once he hears that Mieliehe and the others have come over, he is sure to move against us.

sentences.zh: 彼若先據險要，則難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: If they first seize strategic passes, it will be hard to contend with them.
translations.idiomatic: If he seizes the strong points first, we shall be hard pressed to fight him.

sentences.zh: 今以乜列河等餌之，當競來抄掠，然後設伏以待，必指掌破之。

translations.literal: Now use Mieliehe and the others as bait; they will surely rush to raid; then set an ambush and wait—we are certain to crush them as easily as turning one's palm.
translations.idiomatic: Use Mieliehe and his people as bait; he will rush to plunder them. Then lay an ambush and wait, and we can break him as easily as turning the hand.

sentences.zh: 」廣陽然其計。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Guangyang approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince of Guangyang approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 拔陵果來要擊，破乜列河於嶺上，部衆皆沒。

translations.literal: Balang did come to intercept, defeated Mieliehe on the ridge, and his entire force was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Balang did come to attack, routed Mieliehe on the ridge, and wiped out his whole band.

sentences.zh: 謹伏兵發，賊遂大敗，悉收得乜列河之衆。

translations.literal: Jin's hidden troops sprang up; the rebels were utterly defeated, and he fully recovered Mieliehe's force.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin's hidden troops then rose; the rebels were routed, and he recovered all of Mieliehe's followers.

sentences.zh: 魏帝嘉之，除積射將軍。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor commended him and appointed him General of Accumulating Shots.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor commended him and made him General of Accumulating Shots.

sentences.zh: 太祖臨夏州，以謹為防城大都督，兼夏州長史。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor arrived at Xia Province, he made Jin Grand Commander for Defense of the City and concurrently chief clerk of Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai arrived at Xia Province, he made Yu Jin grand commander for defense of the city and concurrently chief clerk of Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 及岳被害，太祖赴平涼。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed, the Grand Progenitor went to Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue was killed, Yuwen Tai went to Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 謹乃言於太祖曰：「魏祚陵遲，權臣擅命，羣盜蜂起，黔首嗷然。

translations.literal: Jin then spoke to the Grand Progenitor, saying: "The Wei dynasty's fortune declines; powerful ministers seize authority at will; bandits swarm like bees; the common people wail.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin then said to Yuwen Tai: "The Wei house is failing; powerful ministers do as they please; bandits rise everywhere; the people cry out in distress.

sentences.zh: 明公仗超世之姿，懷濟時之略，四方遠近，咸所歸心。

translations.literal: Your Excellency bears a transcendent bearing and holds a strategy to save the age; near and far, all turn their hearts toward you.
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency has a surpassing stature and a plan to rescue the times; men near and far all look to you.

sentences.zh: 願早建良圖，以副衆望。

translations.literal: I wish you would early form a good plan to answer the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to form a worthy design early and answer what the realm expects.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「何以言之？

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor said: "Why do you say so?
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Tai said: "Why do you say that?

sentences.zh: 」謹對曰：「關右，秦漢舊都，古稱天府，將士驍勇，厥壤膏腴，西有巴蜀之饒，北有羊馬之利。

translations.literal: " Jin replied: "Guanzhong—the old capital of Qin and Han, anciently called the Storehouse of Heaven—has fierce brave officers and soldiers and fertile soil; to the west lies the wealth of Ba and Shu, to the north the advantage of sheep and horses.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu Jin answered: "Guanzhong was the old capital of Qin and Han and was called the Storehouse of Heaven. Its soldiers are brave, its soil rich; to the west lie the riches of Ba and Shu, to the north the profit of sheep and horses.

sentences.zh: 今若據其要害，招集英雄，養卒勸農，足觀時變。

translations.literal: If you now hold its strategic points, gather heroes, raise troops and encourage farming, it is enough to watch changes in the times.
translations.idiomatic: If you now hold its key positions, gather heroes, train troops, and encourage farming, you will be able to watch how affairs turn.

sentences.zh: 且天子在洛，逼迫羣兇，若陳明公之懇誠，算時事之利害，請都關右，帝必嘉而西遷。

translations.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven is at Luoyang, pressed by a host of villains; if you set forth Your Excellency's earnest sincerity, calculate the profit and loss of the times, and request that the capital be moved to Guanzhong, the Emperor will surely approve and move west.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven is at Luoyang, hard pressed by a crowd of villains. If you lay out your earnest loyalty, weigh the times, and ask that the court move to Guanzhong, the emperor will surely approve and come west.

sentences.zh: 然後挾天子而令諸侯，奉王命以討暴亂，桓、文之業，千載一時也。

translations.literal: Then, holding the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords and carrying the royal mandate to punish violent disorder—the achievement of Huan and Wen comes but once in a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Then, holding the Son of Heaven to command the lords and carrying the royal mandate to punish disorder, you may do what Huan and Wen did—a chance that comes once in a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 」太祖大悅。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Tai was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 會有勑追謹為

translations.literal: Just then there came an edict recalling Jin to
translations.idiomatic: Just then an edict arrived recalling Yu Jin as

translations.literal: (Guan)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Guan]

sentences.zh: 〔閤〕內大都督，謹因進都關中之策，魏帝納之。

translations.literal: [He] grand commander within the Palace Gate; Jin thereupon advanced the plan to move the capital to Guanzhong, and the Wei Emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander within the Palace Gate; Yu Jin thereupon advanced the plan to move the capital to Guanzhong, and the Wei emperor accepted it.

sentences.zh: 尋而齊神武逼洛陽，謹從魏帝西遷。

translations.literal: Soon Gao Huan pressed on Luoyang, and Jin followed the Wei Emperor in moving west.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gao Huan pressed on Luoyang, and Yu Jin followed the Wei emperor west.

sentences.zh: 仍從太祖征潼關，破回洛城，授使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、北雍州刺史，進爵藍田縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He then followed the Grand Progenitor in campaigning against Tong Pass, captured Huiluo city, was given full credentials, made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Three Divisions Court Equipage, and governor of north Yong Province, advanced in rank to Duke of Lantian county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai against Tong Pass, took Huiluo, and was made commissioner with full credentials, grand general of chariots and cavalry, three-division court equipage, and governor of North Yong Province; he was advanced to Duke of Lantian with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，拜驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong, he was appointed Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Grand Commander with Three Divisions Court Equipage.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong (535) he was appointed grand general of fast cavalry and grand commander with three-division court equipage.

sentences.zh: 其年，夏陽人王遊浪聚據楊氏壁謀逆，謹討擒之。

translations.literal: That same year, Wang Youlang of Xiayang gathered forces and held Yangshi Rampart plotting rebellion; Jin marched against him and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Youlang of Xiayang gathered men, seized Yangshi Rampart, and plotted rebellion; Yu Jin attacked and captured him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大軍東伐，謹為前鋒。

translations.literal: That year the great army marched east to attack; Jin served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: That year the main army marched east, with Yu Jin as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 至盤豆，東魏將高叔禮守險不下，攻破之。

translations.literal: Reaching Pansou, Eastern Wei general Gao Shuli held the passes and would not yield; they stormed and took it.
translations.idiomatic: At Pansou, Eastern Wei general Gao Shuli held the heights and would not come down; they stormed and took the place.

sentences.zh: 拔虜其卒

translations.literal: They stormed it and captured the troops
translations.idiomatic: They stormed it and captured the troops
[variant: 又]

sentences.zh: 〔一千〕。

translations.literal: [one thousand].
translations.idiomatic: numbering one thousand.

sentences.zh: 因此拔弘農，擒東魏陝州刺史李

translations.literal: Thereupon they stormed Hongnong and captured Eastern Wei Shaan Province governor Li
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they took Hongnong and captured Eastern Wei governor of Shaan Province Li

translations.literal: (Zheng)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Zheng]

sentences.zh: 〔徽〕伯。

translations.literal: [Hui] Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Huibo.

sentences.zh: 齊神武至沙苑，謹從太祖與諸將力戰，破之，進爵常山郡公，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Gao Huan reached Shayuan; Jin followed the Grand Progenitor and the various generals in fierce battle and defeated him; he advanced in rank to Duke of Changshan commandery with an additional fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan reached Shayuan, Yu Jin followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and the other generals in hard fighting and routed him; Yu Jin was advanced to Duke of Changshan with an added fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 又從戰河橋。

translations.literal: He again followed in the battle at He Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He again fought at He Bridge.

sentences.zh: 拜大丞相府長史，兼大行臺尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief clerk of the Grand Chancellor's office and concurrently vice director of the Grand Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief clerk of the grand chancellor's office and concurrently vice director of the grand office.

sentences.zh: 稽胡帥夏州刺史劉平叛，謹率衆討平之。

translations.literal: The Jiihu chieftain Liu Ping, governor of Xia Province, rebelled; Jin led troops to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji Hu chieftain Liu Ping, governor of Xia Province, rebelled; Yu Jin led troops and put the rebellion down.

sentences.zh: 除大都督、恆幷燕肆雲五州諸軍事、大將軍、恆州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand commander, supervisor of military affairs in the five provinces of Heng, Bing, Yan, Xi, and Yun, grand general, and governor of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand commander, supervisor of military affairs in the five provinces of Heng, Bing, Yan, Xi, and Yun, grand general, and governor of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 入為太子太師。

translations.literal: He entered court as grand tutor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as grand tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 九年，復從太祖東征，別攻柏谷塢，拔之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again followed the Grand Progenitor on an eastern campaign, separately attacked Baigu Stockade, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he again followed Yuwen Tai east, separately attacked Baigu Stockade, and took it.

sentences.zh: 邙山之戰，大軍不利，謹率其麾下偽降，立於路左。

translations.literal: At the battle of Mount Mang the great army fared badly; Jin led his personal troops in feigned surrender and stood on the left of the road.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Mount Mang the main army was beaten; Yu Jin led his own troops in feigned surrender and stood at the left of the road.

sentences.zh: 齊神武軍乘勝逐北，不以為虞。

translations.literal: Gao Huan's army, riding victory in pursuit, did not take precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan's army, pressing the victory in pursuit, took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 追騎過盡，謹乃自後擊之，敵人大駭。

translations.literal: When the pursuing horsemen had all passed, Jin then struck from the rear, and the enemy was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the pursuers had all passed, Yu Jin struck from the rear and threw the enemy into alarm.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信又集兵士於後奮擊，齊神武軍遂亂，以此大軍得全。

translations.literal: Dugu Xin also gathered troops and fiercely attacked from the rear; Gao Huan's army was thrown into disorder, and thus the great army was saved.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin also rallied troops and attacked fiercely from behind; Gao Huan's army broke into disorder, and by this the main force was saved.

sentences.zh: 十二年，拜尚書左僕射，領司農卿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrently minister of the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made left vice director of the masters of writing and concurrently minister of the directorate of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 及侯景款附，請兵為援，太祖命李弼率兵應之。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing came over in surrender and requested troops as aid, the Grand Progenitor ordered Li Bi to lead troops to respond.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing offered submission and asked for troops as aid, Yuwen Tai ordered Li Bi to lead a force to him.

sentences.zh: 謹諫曰：「侯景少習兵權，情實難測。

translations.literal: Jin remonstrated, saying: "Hou Jing from youth has been versed in military command; his disposition is truly hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin remonstrated, saying: "Hou Jing has known military command since youth; his true intent is hard to read.

sentences.zh: 且宜厚其禮秩，以觀其變。

translations.literal: For now it is fitting to enrich his honors and salary and watch how he changes.
translations.idiomatic: For now we should enrich his honors and salary and watch how he turns.

sentences.zh: 卽欲遣兵，良用未可。

translations.literal: Even if one wishes to send troops, it truly cannot yet be done.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we mean to send troops, it truly is not yet the time.

sentences.zh: 」太祖不聽。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Tai did not listen.

sentences.zh: 尋復兼大行臺尚書、丞相府長史，率兵鎮潼關，加授華州刺史，贈秬鬯一卣，圭瓚副焉。

translations.literal: Soon he again served concurrently as vice director of the Grand Office and chief clerk of the chancellor's office, led troops to garrison Tong Pass, was additionally given governor of Hua Province, and granted one jar of dark spirits with a jade tablet and libation cup to match.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again served concurrently as vice director of the grand office and chief clerk of the chancellor's office, led troops to garrison Tong Pass, was additionally made governor of Hua Province, and was granted one jar of dark spirits with a jade tablet and libation cup to match.

sentences.zh: 俄拜司空，增邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Works with an added fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made minister of works, with an added fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十五年，進位柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he advanced to the rank of Pillar of State grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was advanced to pillar-of-state grand general.

sentences.zh: 齊氏稱帝，太祖征之，以謹為後軍大都督。

translations.literal: When Qi proclaimed an emperor, the Grand Progenitor campaigned against them and made Jin grand commander of the rear army.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi declared an emperor, Yuwen Tai marched against them and made Yu Jin grand commander of the rear army.

sentences.zh: 別封一子鹽亭縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Separately one of his sons was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yanting county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: One of his sons was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Yanting with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，除雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was appointed governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei (554) he was made governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 初，梁元帝平侯景之後，於江陵嗣位，密與齊氏通使，將謀侵軼。

translations.literal: Initially, after Emperor Yuan of Liang pacified Hou Jing, he succeeded to the throne at Jiangling, secretly exchanged envoys with Qi, and planned to raid and invade.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Emperor Yuan of Liang had put down Hou Jing and succeeded at Jiangling, he secretly exchanged envoys with Northern Qi and planned invasion.

sentences.zh: 其兄子岳陽王詧時為雍州刺史，以梁元帝殺〔其〕兄譽，遂結讐隙。

translations.literal: His nephew Prince Xiangyang Xiao Cha was then governor of Yong Province; because Emperor Yuan of Liang had killed [his] elder brother Yu, he thereby formed a feud.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Prince Xiangyang Xiao Cha was then governor of Yong Province; because Emperor Yuan of Liang had killed his elder brother Xiao Yu, they became enemies.

sentences.zh: 據襄陽來附，仍請王師。

translations.literal: He held Xiangyang and came over in allegiance, and also requested imperial troops.
translations.idiomatic: He held Xiangyang, came over in allegiance, and also asked for imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 乃令謹率衆出討。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jin was ordered to lead troops out to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin was then ordered to lead troops out against him.

sentences.zh: 太祖餞於青泥谷。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor saw him off at Qingni Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai saw him off at Qingni Valley.

sentences.zh: 長孫儉問謹曰：「為蕭繹之計，將欲如何？

translations.literal: Zhangsun Jian asked Jin: "As for Xiao Yi's plans, what will he do?
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Jian asked Yu Jin: "What do you think Xiao Yi will do?

sentences.zh: 」謹曰：「耀兵漢、沔，席捲渡江，直據丹陽，是其上策；

translations.literal: " Jin said: "To display troops on the Han and Mian, sweep across the river and directly seize Danyang—that is his best strategy;
translations.idiomatic: " Yu Jin said: "To show force on the Han and Mian, sweep across the river, and seize Danyang directly—that is his best plan;

sentences.zh: 移郭內居民，退保子城，峻其陴堞，以待援至，是其中策；

translations.literal: to move residents within the outer city into the inner citadel, strengthen the walls and towers, and await relief—that is his middle strategy;
translations.idiomatic: to move the people inside the outer walls into the inner citadel, strengthen the ramparts, and wait for aid—that is his middle plan;

sentences.zh: 若難於移動，據守羅郭，是其下策。

translations.literal: if movement is difficult, to hold the outer walls—that is his worst strategy.
translations.idiomatic: if moving them is hard, to hold only the outer walls—that is his worst plan.

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「揣繹定出何策？

translations.literal: " Jian said: "Which strategy do you reckon Yi will choose?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhangsun Jian said: "Which plan do you think Yi will take?

sentences.zh: 」謹曰：「必用下策。

translations.literal: " Jin said: "He will surely use the worst strategy.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu Jin said: "He will surely take the worst plan.

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「彼棄上而用下，何也？

translations.literal: " Jian said: "Why will he abandon the best and use the worst?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhangsun Jian said: "Why would he abandon the best and use the worst?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「蕭氏保據江南，綿歷數紀。

translations.literal: " He replied: "The Xiao clan has held the Yangzi south for many generations.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "The Xiao house has held the south for many generations.

sentences.zh: 屬中原多故，未遑外略。

translations.literal: Just when the central plains had many troubles, they had no leisure for outward expansion.
translations.idiomatic: While the central plains were in constant trouble, they had no leisure for outward campaigns.

sentences.zh: 又以我有齊氏之患，必謂力不能分。

translations.literal: They also think that because we have trouble from Qi, we surely cannot divide our forces.
translations.idiomatic: They also think that because we have trouble from Northern Qi, we cannot spare troops.

sentences.zh: 且繹懦而無謀，多疑少斷。

translations.literal: Moreover Yi is timid and without strategy, suspicious and slow to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yi is timid and unresourceful, suspicious and slow to decide.

sentences.zh: 愚民難與慮始，皆戀邑居，旣惡遷移，當保羅郭。

translations.literal: Ordinary people are hard to move at the start; all cling to their homes; hating relocation, they will hold the outer walls.
translations.idiomatic: Common people are hard to move at the start; they all cling to their homes and hate being uprooted, so he will keep the outer walls.

sentences.zh: 所以用下策也。

translations.literal: That is why he will use the worst strategy.
translations.idiomatic: That is why he will take the worst plan.

sentences.zh: 」謹乃令中山公護及大將軍楊忠等，率精騎先據江津，斷其走路。

translations.literal: " Jin then ordered Duke of Zhongshan Yuwen Hu and Grand General Yang Zhong and others to lead elite cavalry first to seize the Jiang crossing and cut off his escape route.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu Jin then ordered Duke of Zhongshan Yuwen Hu, Grand General Yang Zhong, and others to lead picked cavalry first to hold the river crossing at Jiangling and cut off his escape.

sentences.zh: 梁人豎木柵於外城，廣輪六十里。

translations.literal: The Liang people raised wooden palisades around the outer city, spanning sixty li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang forces raised wooden palisades around the outer city, sixty li around.

sentences.zh: 尋而謹至，悉衆圍之。

translations.literal: Before long Jin arrived and with his full force besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yu Jin arrived and besieged it with his whole force.

sentences.zh: 梁主屢遣兵于城南出戰，輒為謹所破。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler repeatedly sent troops out to fight south of the city and was each time defeated by Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler repeatedly sent troops out to fight south of the city and was beaten each time by Yu Jin.

sentences.zh: 旬有六日，外城遂陷。

translations.literal: After sixteen days the outer city fell.
translations.idiomatic: After sixteen days the outer city fell.

sentences.zh: 梁主退保子城。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler retreated to hold the inner citadel.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler withdrew into the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 翌日，率其太子以下，面縛出降，尋殺之。

translations.literal: The next day he led the crown prince and those below, bound facing forward, to surrender; soon he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he led the crown prince and his household out, bound with faces covered, to surrender; soon he was killed.

sentences.zh: 虜其男女十餘萬人，收其府庫珍寶。
