translations.literal: They captured more than one hundred thousand men and women and seized the treasures of the imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: They took more than one hundred thousand men and women captive and seized the treasures of the palace stores.

sentences.zh: 得宋渾天儀、梁日晷銅表、魏相風烏、銅蟠螭

translations.literal: They obtained the Song armillary sphere, the Liang bronze sundial pillar, the Wei wind-indicating bird, and a bronze coiled dragon
translations.idiomatic: They obtained the Song armillary sphere, the Liang bronze sundial pillar, the Wei wind-indicating bird, and a bronze coiled dragon
[variant: 跌]

sentences.zh: 〔趺〕、大玉徑四尺圍七尺、及諸轝輦法物以獻，軍無私焉。

translations.literal: [base], a great jade disk four feet across and seven feet in circumference, and all ceremonial chariots and ritual objects to present as tribute; the army took nothing for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: pedestal, a great jade disk four feet across and seven feet in circumference, and all ceremonial chariots and ritual objects to present as tribute; the army took nothing for private gain.

sentences.zh: 立蕭詧為梁主，振旅而旋。

translations.literal: They established Xiao Cha as ruler of Liang and, gathering the troops, returned.
translations.idiomatic: They set up Xiao Cha as ruler of Liang and marched home.

sentences.zh: 太祖親至其第，宴語極歡。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor personally came to his residence; the banquet and conversation were exceedingly joyous.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai came in person to his house; the banquet and talk were exceedingly warm.

sentences.zh: 賞謹奴婢一千口，及梁之寶物，幷金石絲竹樂一部，別封新野郡公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He rewarded Jin with one thousand slaves, Liang treasures, and an entire set of metal, stone, string, and bamboo instruments; separately he enfeoffed him as Duke of Xinye commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded Yu Jin with one thousand slaves, Liang treasures, and a full set of metal, stone, string, and bamboo instruments; separately he enfeoffed him as Duke of Xinye with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 謹固辭，太祖不許。

translations.literal: Jin firmly declined; the Grand Progenitor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin firmly declined; Yuwen Tai would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 又令司樂作《常山公平梁歌》十首，使工人歌之。

translations.literal: He also had the Directorate of Music compose ten songs, "Lord Changshan's Pacification of Liang," and had musicians sing them.
translations.idiomatic: He also had the directorate of music compose ten songs, "Lord Changshan's Pacification of Liang," and had musicians sing them.

sentences.zh: 謹自以久當權勢，位望隆重，功名旣立，願保優閑。

translations.literal: Jin himself felt that having long held power, his rank and standing were weighty and his merit and fame already established; he wished to preserve ease and leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin felt that having long held power, with rank and standing already great and merit and fame established, he wished to keep his ease.

sentences.zh: 乃上先所乘駿馬及所著鎧甲等。

translations.literal: Thereupon he presented the fine horses he had ridden and the armor he had worn.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon presented the fine horses he had ridden and the armor he had worn.

sentences.zh: 太祖識其意，乃曰：「今巨猾未平，公豈得便爾獨善。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor understood his intent and said: "Now the great villain is not yet pacified—how can you alone seek ease so soon?
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai understood his meaning and said: "The great villain is not yet subdued—how can you alone seek ease so soon?

sentences.zh: 」遂不受。

translations.literal: " He thereupon did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon would not accept them.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜大司徒。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, Jin was appointed Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was made grand minister of education.

sentences.zh: 及太祖崩，孝閔帝尚幼，中山公護雖受顧命，而名位素下，羣公各圖執政，莫相率服。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor died, Emperor Xiaomin was still young; though Duke of Zhongshan Yuwen Hu had received the dying charge, his name and rank had always been lower, and the various lords each plotted to hold power, none deferring to another.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai died, Emperor Xiaomin was still young; though Duke of Zhongshan Yuwen Hu had received the dying charge, his rank had always been lower, and the great lords each plotted to hold power, none willing to defer.

sentences.zh: 護深憂之，密訪於謹。

translations.literal: Hu was deeply troubled and secretly consulted Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu was deeply troubled and secretly consulted Yu Jin.

sentences.zh: 謹曰：「夙蒙丞相殊睠，情深骨肉。

translations.literal: Jin said: "Since long ago I have received the chancellor's extraordinary favor; our bond is as close as flesh and bone.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin said: "Long ago I received the chancellor's extraordinary favor; our bond is as close as flesh and bone.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，必以死爭之。

translations.literal: Today's matter I will surely contest with my life.
translations.idiomatic: In today's matter I will surely contend with my life.

sentences.zh: 若對衆定策，公必不得辭讓。

translations.literal: If strategy is settled before the assembled lords, you absolutely must not decline.
translations.idiomatic: If the decision is made before the assembled lords, you absolutely must not decline.

sentences.zh: 」明日，羣公會議。

translations.literal: " The next day, the assembled nobles met in council.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, the assembled nobles met in council.

sentences.zh: 謹曰：「昔帝室傾危，人圖問鼎。

translations.literal: Jin said: "In former times the imperial house was tottering; men plotted to seize the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin said: "In former times the imperial house was tottering and men plotted to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 丞相志在匡救，投袂荷戈，故得國祚中興，羣生遂性。

translations.literal: The chief minister's will was to rescue and restore; he shook his sleeves and took up arms, and thus the dynastic fortune was revived and the people returned to their natures.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister's will was to rescue and restore the realm; he shook off delay and took up arms, and thus the dynasty was revived and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 今上天降禍，奄棄庶寮。

translations.literal: Now Heaven sends calamity and suddenly abandons the multitude of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven sends calamity and has suddenly taken away our leaders.

sentences.zh: 嗣子雖幼，而中山公親則猶子，兼受顧托，軍國之事，理須歸之。

translations.literal: The heir is still young, yet Duke of Zhongshan by kinship is like a son, and together received the dying charge—matters of army and state ought by right to fall to him.
translations.idiomatic: The heir is still young, yet Duke of Zhongshan Yuwen Hu, close in kinship as a son and entrusted at the deathbed, ought by right to take charge of army and state.

sentences.zh: 」辭色抗厲，衆皆悚動。

translations.literal: " His words and bearing were stern and forceful; the assembly all trembled.
translations.idiomatic: His words and bearing were stern and forceful, and the whole assembly trembled.

sentences.zh: 護曰：「此是家事，素雖庸昧，何敢有辭。

translations.literal: Hu said: "This is a family matter; though I am by nature dull and ignorant, how dare I refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu said: "This is a family matter; though I am by nature dull and ignorant, how dare I refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」謹旣太祖等夷，護每申禮敬。

translations.literal: " Jin, since the Grand Progenitor's death, Hu had always shown him ritual respect.
translations.idiomatic: Since Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's death, Yuwen Hu had always shown Yu Jin ritual respect.

sentences.zh: 至是，謹乃趨而言曰：「公若統理軍國，謹等便有所依。

translations.literal: At this point Jin hurried forward and said: "If you take charge of army and state, Jin and the rest will have someone to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Yu Jin hurried forward and said: "If you take charge of army and state, we will have someone to rely on.

sentences.zh: 」遂再拜。

translations.literal: " He thereupon bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 羣公迫於謹，亦再拜，因是衆議始定。

translations.literal: The assembled nobles, pressed by Jin, also bowed twice; thus the assembly's decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled nobles, pressed by Yu Jin, also bowed twice, and the assembly's decision was settled.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進封燕國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Northern Zhou ascended the throne, Jin was advanced to Duke of Yan, fief ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Yu Jin was advanced to Duke of Yan with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 遷太傅、大宗伯，與李弼、侯莫陳崇等參議朝政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand preceptor and grand minister of ritual, and with Li Bi, Houmochen Chong, and others deliberated on court governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand preceptor and grand minister of ritual, and with Li Bi, Houmochen Chong, and others deliberated on court governance.

sentences.zh: 及賀蘭祥討吐谷渾也，謹遙統其軍，授以方略。

translations.literal: When Helan Xiang campaigned against Tuyuhun, Jin directed his army from afar and supplied strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When Helan Xiang campaigned against Tuyuhun, Yu Jin directed his army from afar and supplied strategy.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，謹以年老，上表乞骸骨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding (562), Jin, on account of old age, submitted a memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding (562), Yu Jin, on account of old age, submitted a memorial requesting retirement.

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「昔師尚父年踰九十，召公奭幾將百歲，皆勤王家，自強不息。

translations.literal: An edict replied: "In former times Grand Mentor Shangfu passed ninety years of age, and Duke of Shao She was nearly a hundred; both served the royal house diligently and never ceased to strengthen themselves.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "In former times Grand Mentor Jiang Ziya passed ninety years of age, and Duke of Shao She was nearly a hundred; both served the royal house diligently and never ceased to strengthen themselves.

sentences.zh: 今元惡未除，九州不一，將以公為舟烜，弘濟於艱難，豈容忘二公之雅操，而有斯請。

translations.literal: Now the chief evil is not yet removed and the Nine Provinces are not yet united; I intend to make you the beacon for the vessel and broadly deliver us through hardship—how could I forget those two lords' lofty conduct and grant this request?
translations.idiomatic: Now the chief enemy is not yet removed and the realm is not yet united; I intend to make you the beacon for the vessel and deliver us through hardship—how could I forget those two lords' lofty conduct and grant this request?

sentences.zh: 朕用恧焉。

translations.literal: I am ashamed because of it.
translations.idiomatic: I am ashamed to hear it.

sentences.zh: 公若更執謙沖，有司宜斷啟。」

translations.literal: If you again hold to humility, the responsible offices should reject the memorial."
translations.idiomatic: If you again hold to humility, the responsible offices should reject the memorial."

sentences.zh: 三年四月，詔曰：「樹以元首，主乎教化，率民孝悌，置之仁壽。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, an edict said: "To set up a head is to preside over teaching and transformation, to lead the people in filial piety and brotherliness, and place them in benevolence and long life.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year (563), an edict said: "To set up a head is to preside over teaching and transformation, to lead the people in filial piety and brotherliness, and place them in benevolence and long life.

sentences.zh: 是以古先明後，咸若斯典，立三老五更，躬自袒割。

translations.literal: Therefore ancient wise sovereigns and enlightened rulers all followed this canon, establishing the Elder of State and Elder Emeritus and personally baring the shoulder to carve the meat.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore ancient wise sovereigns and enlightened rulers all followed this canon, establishing the Elder of State and Elder Emeritus and personally baring the shoulder to carve the meat.

sentences.zh: 朕以眇身，處茲南面，何敢遺此黃發，不加尊敬。

translations.literal: I with my slight person stand in this south-facing position—how dare I neglect these white-haired elders and fail to show them respect?
translations.idiomatic: I with my slight person stand in this south-facing position—how dare I neglect these white-haired elders and fail to show them respect?

sentences.zh: 太傅、燕國公謹，執德淳固，為國元老，饋以乞言，朝野所屬。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, Duke of Yan Jin, holds virtue pure and firm, is an elder statesman of the realm, and is looked to for counsel by court and countryside alike.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor, Duke of Yan Yu Jin, holds virtue pure and firm, is an elder statesman of the realm, and is looked to for counsel by court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 可為三老，有司具禮，擇日以聞。

translations.literal: He may serve as Elder of State; the responsible offices should prepare the rites and report the chosen day.
translations.idiomatic: He may serve as Elder of State; the responsible offices should prepare the rites and report the chosen day.

sentences.zh: 」謹上表固辭，詔答不許。

translations.literal: " Jin submitted a memorial firmly declining; the edict in reply would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin submitted a memorial firmly declining; the edict in reply would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 又賜延年杖。

translations.literal: He was also granted a staff of extended years.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted a staff of extended years.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸太學以食之。

translations.literal: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong visited the Imperial Academy to feed him.
translations.idiomatic: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong visited the Imperial Academy to feed him.

sentences.zh: 三老入門，皇帝迎拜門屏之間，三老答拜。

translations.literal: When the Elder of State entered the gate, the emperor welcomed and bowed between the gate and screen; the Elder of State returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the Elder of State entered the gate, the emperor welcomed and bowed between the gate and screen; the Elder of State returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 有司設三老席於中楹，南向。

translations.literal: The responsible offices set the Elder of State's mat at the central pillar, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices set the Elder of State's mat at the central pillar, facing south.

sentences.zh: 太師、晉國公護升階，設幾

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu ascended the steps and set out a low table
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor, Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu ascended the steps and set out a low table

translations.literal: (Shi)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: 施]

sentences.zh: 〔於〕席。

translations.literal: [At] the seat.
translations.idiomatic: at the seat.

sentences.zh: 三老升席，南面憑几而坐，以師道自居。

translations.literal: The Elder of State ascended the mat, sat facing south leaning on the low table, and took the teacher's position.
translations.idiomatic: The Elder of State ascended the mat, sat facing south leaning on the low table, and took the teacher's position.

sentences.zh: 大司

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Justice
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Justice

translations.literal: (Ma)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: 馬]

sentences.zh: 〔寇〕、楚國公寧升階，正舄。

translations.literal: [Kou], Duke of Chu Dou Lü Ning ascended the steps and adjusted his shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Lü Ning, Duke of Chu and grand minister of justice, ascended the steps and adjusted his shoes.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升階，立於斧扆之前，西面。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the steps and stood before the axe-screen, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the steps and stood before the axe-screen, facing west.

sentences.zh: 有司進饌，皇帝跪設醬豆，親自袒割。

translations.literal: The responsible offices brought food; the emperor knelt to set out sauce and beans and personally bared his shoulder to carve the meat.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices brought food; the emperor knelt to set out sauce and beans and personally bared his shoulder to carve the meat.

sentences.zh: 三老食訖，皇帝又親跪授爵以酳。

translations.literal: When the Elder of State had finished eating, the emperor again personally knelt and presented a cup for the rinsing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Elder of State had finished eating, the emperor again personally knelt and presented a cup for the rinsing.

sentences.zh: 有司撤訖。

translations.literal: The responsible offices cleared away.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices cleared away.

sentences.zh: 皇帝北面立而訪道。

translations.literal: The emperor stood facing north and inquired about the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stood facing north and inquired about the Way.

sentences.zh: 三老乃起立於席後。

translations.literal: The Elder of State then rose and stood behind the mat.
translations.idiomatic: The Elder of State then rose and stood behind the mat.

sentences.zh: 皇帝曰：「猥當天下重任，自惟不才，不知政治之要，公其誨之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I unworthily bear the realm's heavy charge; considering myself without talent, I do not know the essentials of governance—please instruct me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I unworthily bear the realm's heavy charge; considering myself without talent, I do not know the essentials of governance—please instruct me.

sentences.zh: 」三老答曰：「木受繩則正，後從諫則聖。

translations.literal: " The Elder of State replied: "Wood that receives the line becomes straight; a ruler who follows remonstrance becomes sage.
translations.idiomatic: The Elder of State replied: "Wood that receives the line becomes straight; a ruler who follows remonstrance becomes sage.

sentences.zh: 自古明王聖主，皆虛心納諫，以知得失，天下乃安。

translations.literal: From antiquity enlightened kings and sage sovereigns all received advice with an open mind to know gain and loss, and only then was the realm secure.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity enlightened kings and sage sovereigns all received advice with an open mind to know gain and loss, and only then was the realm secure.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下念之。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty keep this in mind.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty keep this in mind.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「為國之本，在乎忠信。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The root of governing a state lies in loyalty and trust.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The root of governing a state lies in loyalty and trust.

sentences.zh: 是以古人雲去食去兵，信不可失。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients said that though food and arms may be set aside, trust must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the ancients said that though food and arms may be set aside, trust must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 國家興廢，莫不由之。

translations.literal: Whether a state rises or falls, none is without this.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a state rises or falls, none is without this.

sentences.zh: 願陛下守而勿失。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty hold to it and not lose it.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty hold to it and not lose it.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「治國之道，必須有法。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The way to govern a state must have law.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The way to govern a state must have law.

sentences.zh: 法者，國之綱紀。

translations.literal: Law is the state's cord and net.
translations.idiomatic: Law is the state's cord and net.

sentences.zh: 綱紀不可不正，所正在於賞罰。

translations.literal: The cord and net cannot fail to be straight; what makes them straight lies in reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The cord and net cannot fail to be straight; what makes them straight lies in reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 若有功必賞，有罪必罰，則有善者日益，為惡者日止。

translations.literal: If merit is always rewarded and guilt always punished, then those who do good daily increase and those who do evil daily cease.
translations.idiomatic: If merit is always rewarded and guilt always punished, then those who do good daily increase and those who do evil daily cease.

sentences.zh: 若有功不賞，有罪不罰，則天下善惡不分，下民無所措其手足矣。

translations.literal: If merit is not rewarded and guilt is not punished, then good and evil in the realm are not distinguished and the common people have nowhere to set hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: If merit is not rewarded and guilt is not punished, then good and evil in the realm are not distinguished and the common people have nowhere to set hand or foot.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「言行者立身之基，言出行隨，誠宜相顧。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Words and conduct are the foundation of establishing the person; words go out and conduct follows—one should truly look to both.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Words and conduct are the foundation of establishing the person; words go out and conduct follows—one should truly look to both.

sentences.zh: 願陛下三思而言，九慮而行。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty think thrice before speaking and consider nine times before acting.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty think thrice before speaking and consider nine times before acting.

sentences.zh: 若不思不慮，必有過失。

translations.literal: If one does not think and does not consider, there will surely be fault.
translations.idiomatic: If one does not think and does not consider, there will surely be fault.

sentences.zh: 天子之過，事無大小，如日月之蝕，莫不知者。

translations.literal: A son of Heaven's fault, whether the matter be large or small, is like an eclipse of sun or moon—none do not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: A son of Heaven's fault, whether the matter be large or small, is like an eclipse of sun or moon—none do not know of it.

sentences.zh: 願陛下慎之。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty be careful.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty be careful.

sentences.zh: 」三老言畢，皇帝再拜受之，三老答拜焉。

translations.literal: " When the Elder of State had finished speaking, the emperor bowed twice to receive it, and the Elder of State returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the Elder of State had finished speaking, the emperor bowed twice to receive it, and the Elder of State returned the bow.

sentences.zh: 禮成而出。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 謹有智謀，善於事上。

translations.literal: Jin had wisdom and stratagem and was skilled at serving his superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin had wisdom and stratagem and was skilled at serving his superiors.

sentences.zh: 名位雖重，愈存謙挹。

translations.literal: Though his name and rank were weighty, he preserved humility all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Though his name and rank were weighty, he preserved humility all the more.

sentences.zh: 每朝參往來，不過從兩三騎而已。

translations.literal: Each time he came and went to court audience, he had no more than two or three mounted attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he came and went to court audience, he had no more than two or three mounted attendants.

sentences.zh: 朝廷凡有軍國之務，多與謹決之。

translations.literal: Whenever the court had matters of army and state, they were mostly decided with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court had matters of army and state, they were mostly decided with Yu Jin.

sentences.zh: 謹亦竭其智能，弼諧帝室。

translations.literal: Jin also exhausted his wisdom and ability to harmonize and assist the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin also exhausted his wisdom and ability to harmonize and assist the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 故功臣之中，特見委信，始終若一，人無間言。

translations.literal: Therefore among the meritorious ministers he was especially entrusted and trusted, from beginning to end as one, and no one spoke against him.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore among the meritorious ministers he was especially entrusted and trusted, from beginning to end as one, and no one spoke against him.

sentences.zh: 每教訓諸子，務存靜退。

translations.literal: Whenever he instructed his sons, he urged them to preserve quiet withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he instructed his sons, he urged them to preserve quiet withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 加以年齒遐長，禮遇隆重，子孫繁衍，皆至顯達，當時莫與為比焉。

translations.literal: Added to this, his years were very long and his honors heavy; his descendants multiplied and all reached eminence—at the time none could compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this, his years were very long and his honors heavy; his descendants multiplied and all reached eminence—at the time none could compare with him.

sentences.zh: 子寔嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 寔字賓實，少和厚。

translations.literal: Shi, styled Binshen, in youth was gentle and generous.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, styled Binshen, in youth was gentle and generous.

sentences.zh: 年未弱冠，入太祖幕府，從征潼關及回洛城。

translations.literal: Before he had reached capped age, he entered the Grand Progenitor's headquarters and followed in the campaigns at Tong Pass and Huiluo city.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had reached capped age, he entered Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's headquarters and followed in the campaigns at Tong Pass and Huiluo city.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，又從復弘農，戰沙苑。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong (537), he again followed in recovering Hongnong and fighting at Shawei.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong (537), he again followed in recovering Hongnong and fighting at Shawei.

sentences.zh: 以前後功，封萬年縣子，邑五百戶，授主衣都統。

translations.literal: For earlier and later merit, he was enfeoffed Viscount of Wannian county, fief five hundred households, and appointed chief of the imperial wardrobe corps.
translations.idiomatic: For earlier and later merit, he was enfeoffed Viscount of Wannian county with a fief of five hundred households and appointed chief of the imperial wardrobe corps.

sentences.zh: 河橋之役，先鋒陷陣。

translations.literal: In the battle at Heqiao, as vanguard he broke the enemy line.
translations.idiomatic: In the battle at Heqiao, as vanguard he broke the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 軍還，寔又為內殿，除通直散騎常侍，轉太子右衛率，加都督。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Shi again served in the inner palace; he was appointed directly-attendant scattered-cavalry regular attendant, transferred to right commandant of the crown prince's guard, and given governor-general rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Shi again served in the inner palace; he was appointed directly-attendant scattered-cavalry regular attendant, transferred to right commandant of the crown prince's guard, and given governor-general rank.

sentences.zh: 又從太祖戰於邙山。

translations.literal: He again followed the Grand Progenitor in battle at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in battle at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔寔侍講東宮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, an edict ordered Shi to lecture in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (545), an edict ordered Shi to lecture in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 侯景來附，遣寔與諸軍援之，平九曲城。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing came to submit, Shi was sent with the various armies to aid him and pacified Jiuchu city.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing came to submit, Shi was sent with the various armies to aid him and pacified Jiuchu city.

sentences.zh: 進大都督，遷儀同三司，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to great governor-general, transferred to commissioner equal to three ministers, and given scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to great governor-general, transferred to commissioner equal to three ministers, and given scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 十四年，除尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was appointed minister of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (548), he was appointed minister of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 是歲，太祖與魏太子西巡，寔時從。

translations.literal: That year the Grand Progenitor and the Wei crown prince toured west; Shi followed at the time.
translations.idiomatic: That year Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and the Wei crown prince toured west; Shi followed at the time.

sentences.zh: 太祖刻石於隴山之上，錄功臣位，以次鐫勒，預以寔為開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor carved stone on Mount Long, recording the meritorious ministers' ranks and inscribing them in order; Shi was provisionally listed as commissioner with privilege to open an office equal to three ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai carved stone on Mount Long, recording the meritorious ministers' ranks and inscribing them in order; Shi was provisionally listed as commissioner with privilege to open an office equal to three ministers.

sentences.zh: 至十五年，方授之。

translations.literal: Only in the fifteenth year was it formally granted.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the fifteenth year (549) was it formally granted.

sentences.zh: 尋除滑州刺史，特給鼓吹一部，進爵為公，增邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Hua Province, specially granted one set of drums and pipes, advanced to duke, fief increased by two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed governor of Hua Province, specially granted one set of drums and pipes, advanced to duke, and his fief was increased by two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，羌東念姐率部落反，結連吐谷渾，每為邊患。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei (555), the Qiang Dong Nianjie led his tribes in rebellion, linking with Tuyuhun and constantly causing border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei (555), the Qiang chieftain Dong Nianjie led his tribes in rebellion, linking with Tuyuhun and constantly causing border trouble.

sentences.zh: 遣大將軍豆盧甯討之，踰時不克。

translations.literal: Grand General Dou Lü Ning was sent to suppress them; after more than the allotted time he could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Dou Lü Ning was sent to suppress them; after more than the allotted time he could not overcome them.

sentences.zh: 又令寔往，遂破之。

translations.literal: Shi was again ordered to go, and thereupon defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was again ordered to go, and thereupon defeated them.

sentences.zh: 太祖手書勞問，賜奴婢一百口，馬一百疋。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor wrote a letter in his own hand to express sympathy and inquiry, and granted one hundred household slaves and one hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai wrote a letter in his own hand to express sympathy and inquiry, and granted one hundred household slaves and one hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐祚，授民部中大夫，進爵延壽郡公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Shi was appointed grand master of the ministry of the people, advanced to Duke of Yanshou commandery, fief two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Shi was appointed grand master of the ministry of the people, advanced to Duke of Yanshou commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 又進位大將軍，除勳州刺史，入為小司寇。

translations.literal: He was again advanced to grand general, appointed governor of Xun Province, and entered court as lesser minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was again advanced to grand general, appointed governor of Xun Province, and entered court as lesser minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，延州蒲川賊郝三郎等反，攻逼丹州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe (567), the Puchuan bandits of Yan Province, Hao Sanlang and others, rebelled and pressed Dan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhe (567), the Puchuan bandits of Yan Province, Hao Sanlang and others, rebelled and pressed Dan Province.

sentences.zh: 遣寔率衆討平之，斬三郎首，獲雜畜萬餘頭。

translations.literal: Shi was sent leading troops to suppress and pacify them, beheaded Sanlang, and captured more than ten thousand head of mixed livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was sent leading troops to suppress and pacify them, beheaded Sanlang, and captured more than ten thousand head of mixed livestock.

sentences.zh: 乃除延州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then appointed governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 五年，襲爵燕國公，進位柱國，以罪免。

translations.literal: In the fifth year (570), he inherited the title Duke of Yan, was advanced to pillar of state, and was dismissed for crime.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (570), he inherited the title Duke of Yan, was advanced to pillar of state, and was dismissed for crime.

sentences.zh: 尋復本官，除涼州總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored to his former office and appointed commander-in-chief of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored to his former office and appointed commander-in-chief of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 大象二年，加上柱國，拜大左輔。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daxiang (580), he was given superior pillar of state and appointed grand left aide.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daxiang (580), he was given superior pillar of state and appointed grand left aide.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇元年，薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Sui Kaihuang (581), he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Sui Kaihuang (581), he died.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，諡曰安。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted minister of works; his posthumous title was An.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted minister of works; his posthumous title was An.

sentences.zh: 子顗，大象末，上開府、吳州總管、新野郡公。

translations.literal: His son Yan, at the end of Daxiang, was superior opener-of-office, commander-in-chief of Wu Province, and Duke of Xinye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin's son Yan, at the end of Daxiang (581), was upper opener-of-gates, commander-in-chief of Wu Province, and Duke of Xinye commandery.

sentences.zh: 顗弟仲文，大將軍、延壽郡公。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Zhongwen was grand general and Duke of Yanshou commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Yu Zhongwen was grand general and Duke of Yanshou commandery.

sentences.zh: 仲文弟象賢，儀同三司，尚高祖女。

translations.literal: Zhongwen's younger brother Xiangxian was privilege equal to three ministers and married Gaozu's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen's younger brother Yu Xiangxian held privilege equal to three ministers and married a daughter of High Ancestor Yuwen Yong.

sentences.zh: 寔弟翼，自有傳。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Yi has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's younger brother Yu Yi has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 翼弟義，上柱國、潼州總管、建平郡公。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Yi was superior pillar of state, commander-in-chief of Tong Province, and Duke of Jianping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Yu Yi was superior pillar of state, commander-in-chief of Tong Province, and Duke of Jianping commandery.

sentences.zh: 義弟禮，上大將軍、趙州刺史、安平郡公。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Li was upper grand general, governor of Zhao Province, and Duke of Anping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Yu Li was upper grand general, governor of Zhao Province, and Duke of Anping commandery.

sentences.zh: 禮弟智，初為開府，以受宣帝旨，告齊王憲反，遂封齊國公。

translations.literal: Li's younger brother Zhi, at first opening-the-feudatory, on receiving Emperor Xuan's command denounced Prince of Qi Xian's rebellion, and was thereupon enfeoffed Duke of Qi state.
translations.idiomatic: Li's younger brother Yu Zhi, at first an opener-of-office, on receiving Emperor Xuan Yuwen Yun's command denounced Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian's rebellion, and was thereupon enfeoffed Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 尋拜柱國、涼州總管、大司空。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed pillar of state, commander-in-chief of Liang Province, and grand minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed pillar of state, commander-in-chief of Liang Province, and grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 智

translations.literal: Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Zhi

translations.literal: (Beginning)
translations.idiomatic: [initial variant]

sentences.zh: 弟紹，上開府、綏州刺史、華陽郡公。

translations.literal: Younger brother Shao was superior opener-of-office, governor of Sui Province, and Duke of Huayang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yu Shao was upper opener-of-gates, governor of Sui Province, and Duke of Huayang commandery.

sentences.zh: 紹弟弼，上儀同、平恩縣公。

translations.literal: Shao's younger brother Bi was upper equal-in-protocol and Duke of Ping'en county.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's younger brother Yu Bi was upper equal-in-protocol and Duke of Ping'en county.

sentences.zh: 弼弟蘭，上儀同、襄陽縣公。

translations.literal: Bi's younger brother Lan was upper equal-in-protocol and Duke of Xiangyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's younger brother Yu Lan was upper equal-in-protocol and Duke of Xiangyang county.

sentences.zh: 蘭弟曠，上儀同，贈恆州刺史。

translations.literal: Lan's younger brother Kuang was upper equal-in-protocol and posthumously granted governor of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: Lan's younger brother Yu Kuang was upper equal-in-protocol and was posthumously made governor of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：賀拔岳變起倉卒，侯莫陳悅意在兼併，于時將有離心，士無固志。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When Heba Yue's mutiny arose in haste, Houmochen Yue intended annexation; at the time the generals had divided hearts and the soldiers lacked firm will.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: When Heba Yue was murdered in sudden turmoil and Houmochen Yue sought to absorb his army, the commanders wavered and the troops had no fixed loyalty.

sentences.zh: 洛撫緝散亂，抗禦仇讐。

translations.literal: Luo soothed and gathered the scattered disorder and resisted the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Luo soothed the scattered host and held off the foe.

sentences.zh: 全師而還，敵人絕覬覦之望；

translations.literal: Returning with the full army, the enemy ceased all hope of coveting;
translations.idiomatic: He brought the whole force back intact, and the enemy lost all hope of gain;

sentences.zh: 度德而處，霸王建匡合之謀。

translations.literal: measuring virtue in his conduct, the hegemon-king established plans for alignment and union.
translations.idiomatic: measuring his own strength, he laid the foundations of the Zhou hegemony.

sentences.zh: 此功故不細也。

translations.literal: This achievement was thus not small.
translations.idiomatic: That was no minor achievement.

sentences.zh: 李弼、于謹懷佐時之略，逢啟聖之運，綢繆顧遇，締構艱難，帷幄盡其謨猷，方面宣其庸績，擬巨川之舟楫，為大廈之棟樑。

translations.literal: Li Bi and Yu Jin harbored the strategy of assisting the age, encountered the fortune of a sage founding, received care and favor, built through hardship, in the tent exhausted their counsel, in the regions displayed their merit—like boat and oar on a great river, pillars and beams for a great edifice.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi and Yu Jin brought timely counsel to a founding age, won favor through loyal service, and built the dynasty through hardship—counsel in the command tent, achievement on the frontier; they were the river craft and the roof beams of the new state.

sentences.zh: 非惟攀附成名，抑亦材謀自取。

translations.literal: Not only by attaching to fame, but also by talent and strategy self-won.
translations.idiomatic: They won renown not merely by riding others' rise, but by their own ability and design.

sentences.zh: 及謹以耆年碩德，譽重望高，禮備上庠，功歌司樂，常以滿盈為戒，覆折是憂。

translations.literal: When Jin, with venerable years and great virtue, reputation heavy and esteem high, rites complete at the upper school, merit sung by the director of music, always took fullness as warning and collapse as concern.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin in old age and great virtue, with weighty reputation and high esteem, honored at the Imperial Academy and celebrated in court music, always took fullness as warning and ruin as his fear.

sentences.zh: 不有君子，何以能國。

translations.literal: Without a gentleman, how can there be a state.
translations.idiomatic: Without such a man, how could the state endure?

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
